answer: Make identity a reef, not a flag: standing accretes only while an identity keeps laying down small, signed verification proofs, checking peers' transactions one after another, each chained to its own history like basalt cooling layer on layer. The proofs are non-transferable and expire fast, so the cost per identity looks velvet-soft, a few minutes of real checking. But it never stops and never batches: a thousand masks demand a thousand identities' worth of continuous work, and any chain left idle crumbles back to zero. Forgery is cheap once; this makes it expensive forever.
